supporting_observations.claim: The periodic outbound connections are attributed to stockpilotupd.exe running as eli.brooks; successful proxy connections to update.stockpilot.co are recorded at 13:39, 13:44, 13:48, 13:54, 14:04, and 14:09 UTC, with a denied attempt at 13:59.
The observed destination is update.stockpilot.co, whereas the inventory identifies update.stockpilot.com as the approved StockPilot update host.
The network-attributed updater runs from eli.brooks's AppData\Local directory, not the inventory-listed approved path under C:\Program Files\StockPilot.

The process created a file at its own executable path shortly after its first observed connection; this is noteworthy alongside the destination and path discrepancies, but does not by itself establish what file content changed.

The combination of a near-five-minute connection cadence, a domain differing from the approved StockPilot host, and execution from a user-profile path supports treating the alerted activity as malicious and escalating it for investigation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records identify the StockPilot hostname and tunnel metadata, but the listed StockPilot connections are CONNECT tunnels; the available records do not show their HTTPS request paths or payload contents.
The evidence does not provide a hash, signature validation, or file contents for the AppData\Local executable.
The records establish observed connections during the supplied window, but do not establish the reputation, ownership, or legitimacy of update.stockpilot.co.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish what data, if any, was sent to or received from update.stockpilot.co.
The evidence does not establish whether the AppData\Local executable is a malicious replacement, an authorized per-user installation, or an undocumented update mechanism.
The evidence does not establish whether the proxy denial at 13:59 was caused by malicious content or by another policy or network condition.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect and preserve the executable and related files from C:\Users\eli.brooks\AppData\Local\StockPilot; obtain hashes, signature status, timestamps, and file provenance.
Review proxy TLS-inspection or endpoint network telemetry, if available, for the content and requests associated with update.stockpilot.co.
Verify the approved StockPilot update domain and installation paths with the software owner or vendor, and check whether this host is authorized to use the observed domain and per-user executable.
unrelated_findings: A PowerShell endpoint-inventory script running as SYSTEM on WS-EBROOKS-01 used explicit svc-inventory credentials. Inventory describes svc-inventory as a FILE-BLU-01 job account; this is separate from the alerted StockPilot connections and should be reviewed independently. (T195-00126, T195-00128)

The domain controller validated a ken.ito authentication from WS-EBROOKS-01, and WS-KITO-01 recorded a network logon for ken.ito from that workstation. This differs from the stated remote-administration practice that administration is performed from WS-KITO-01. (T195-00206, T195-00207)

DropboxUpdate.exe ran on WS-EBROOKS-01; Dropbox is not among the listed approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services. The records show the updater process, not Dropbox data transfer. (T195-00229, T195-00230)

The user launched Cisco AnyConnect's vpnui.exe on WS-EBROOKS-01, although the environment states there is no VPN. These records show a UI process launch, not a VPN connection. (T195-00271, T195-00272)
